steps.description: Load /eval-four-models-v2-with-no-replicates-1v1-s1-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12,000 genes x 2 samples, gene ids in the first column) and /eval-four-models-v2-with-no-replicates-1v1-s1-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (2 rows: sample, condition). steps.name: Normalized counts and descriptive log2 fold changes (no test)
caveats: FLAG (R-0003@6b3a): one sample per condition. No inferential differential expression test may be run; report normalized counts and descriptive log2 fold changes only, state that the design has no replication, and name the design that supports inference (at minimum 3 biological replicates per condition).

The counts come from Salmon as a gene-level table with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, so the import state is not established. Fit on the counts as delivered with no length offset, and state that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as an apparent expression change (R-0169@18ab).

A large log2FC on a low-count gene is dominated by shot noise; the mean-count floor mitigates but does not remove this, and with n=1 per group the technical and biological variance cannot be separated at all.
steps.context: Design: 1 treated vs 1 control human liver sample, raw gene-level counts from Salmon as delivered. The Inflexa procedure flags this design with outcome descriptive_only and drops the shrinkage and multiple-testing steps. The counts' length-correction state is not established and no quant.sf files or average-transcript-length table exist in the inputs.
steps.question: Ranked by descriptive log2 fold change on median-of-ratios normalized counts, which genes differ most between the treated liver sample and the control liver sample - with no p-value, since the design has no replication?

grounding.reason: Flagged by R-0003@6b3a: one sample per condition removes inference, so the step is descriptive_only - median-of-ratios normalized counts and descriptive log2 fold changes, with shrink_lfc and multiple_testing dropped from the procedure.

constraints: Low count filter: keep a gene with at least 10 counts in at least the smallest group size of samples (min_count = 10, min_samples = 1)
Normalization is median-of-ratios size factors applied inside DESeq2; do not pre-normalize the counts (R-0026@9ab1)
Set the reference level explicitly; name the contrast as factor, numerator, denominator (R-0036@9786)
Forbidden methods for this step: DESeq2 Wald test, DESeq2 LRT, edgeR exact test, edgeR quasi-likelihood, limma-voom, and any LFC shrinkage estimator
Use the gene counts as delivered with NO length offset; do not run tximport on a gene-level table and do not invent a transcript-length input (R-0169@18ab)
Candidate threshold for reporting only: |descriptive log2FC| >= 1 and mean normalized count >= 50 - state that this is an arbitrary reporting cut, not a statistical criterion
steps.description: Construct a DESeqDataSet from counts.csv and metadata.csv with design ~ condition. Set the reference level of the condition factor EXPLICITLY to the control level as named in metadata.csv (do not rely on alphabetical ordering), and name the contrast as the triple (condition, treated_level, control_level) so a positive log2 fold change means higher in the treated sample. Apply the low-count filter: keep a gene with at least 10 counts in at least 1 sample (the smallest group size here is 1). Estimate size factors with the median-of-ratios method (estimateSizeFactors) and extract normalized counts. Compute a DESCRIPTIVE log2 fold change per retained gene as log2((normalized_treated + 1) / (normalized_control + 1)); the pseudocount must be stated in the output. Emit a single results table with: gene id, raw counts per sample, normalized counts per sample, mean normalized count, and descriptive log2FC, sorted by descriptive log2FC. Flag the genes with |log2FC| >= 1 AND mean normalized count >= 50 as CANDIDATE genes of interest - label the column 'candidate', never 'significant' or 'DE'. Produce an MA plot and a labelled scatter of normalized counts (treated vs control) highlighting the top 25 up and top 25 down candidates. DO NOT run DESeq(), nfbinomWaldTest, nbinomLRT, edgeR exactTest/glmQLFTest, or limma-voom; DO NOT produce p-values, adjusted p-values, or LFC shrinkage - with one sample per group no dispersion is estimable and any such statistic would be fabricated inference (R-0003@6b3a). Every output file and figure caption must carry the statement that these are descriptive fold changes from an unreplicated design.
acceptance_criteria: No p-value, adjusted p-value, FDR, or shrunken LFC appears anywhere in the outputs
The reference level is set explicitly to the control condition and the contrast is written out as (condition, treated, control) in the output and the log
Size factors are median-of-ratios (estimateSizeFactors) and are reported per sample
The low-count filter (>=10 counts in >=1 sample) is applied and the number of genes retained out of 12,000 is reported
The results table carries raw counts, normalized counts, and descriptive log2FC per gene, with the pseudocount stated
Candidate genes are labelled 'candidate', not 'significant' or 'differentially expressed'

Reproducibility record: session_info, seed, package versions, annotation release if any is used

steps.description: Assemble a markdown report from the T1S1 QC outputs and the T1S2 descriptive table. State, in this order: (1) the limitation first - the design holds one treated and one control human liver sample, there is no biological replication, no dispersion can be estimated, therefore NO gene can be called differentially expressed from these data and no p-values were computed; an inferential answer requires at minimum 3 biological replicates per condition. (2) The method: DESeq2 median-of-ratios size factors, the low-count filter (>=10 counts in >=1 sample), the explicit reference level and the contrast written as (condition, treated, control), the descriptive log2FC formula with its pseudocount, and the arbitrary candidate reporting cut (|log2FC| >= 1, mean normalized count >= 50). (3) The counts-provenance caveat: gene-level counts from Salmon as delivered, length-correction state not established, no length offset applied, isoform-usage shifts can appear as expression changes. (4) The numbers: genes tested/retained out of 12,000, library sizes, size factors, and the count of candidate genes up and down - reported as counts of candidates, never as a count of DE genes. (5) The top 25 up and top 25 down candidate genes as a table, framed as hypotheses to test in a replicated experiment. (6) A reproducibility record: sessionInfo(), all package versions, and any random seed used. No enrichment, no pathway interpretation, and no mechanistic narrative is to be built on this ranking.
acceptance_criteria: The no-replication limitation and the absence of any p-value appear in the first paragraph of the report, before any gene table
The report names the method, every package version, the design formula, the contrast as (condition, treated, control), the reporting thresholds, and the number of genes retained after filtering
Gene counts are reported as 'candidate' counts and the report never states a number of differentially expressed or significant genes
The Salmon length-offset caveat is stated explicitly
A reproducibility record (sessionInfo, package versions, seed) is included with the results

plan.title: Liver treated vs control: descriptive fold changes (n=1 per group)
plan.analytical_narrative: The input is a gene-level count matrix from Salmon (/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv, 12,000 genes x 2 samples) with a 2-row metadata table (/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv) describing one treated and one control human liver sample. The research question asks which genes are differentially expressed between the treated and the control sample. The design has NO biological replication: one sample per condition. Without within-group replication no dispersion can be estimated, so no inferential differential expression test (DESeq2 Wald, edgeR QL/exact, limma-voom) has any inferential basis here; the Inflexa procedure flags this design (R-0003@6b3a) with outcome descriptive_only and drops the LFC-shrinkage and multiple-testing steps entirely. The plan therefore delivers what the data can support and no more: (T1S1) sample-structure QC on the two libraries - library sizes, detected genes, blind VST, and the sample-to-sample distance/correlation on the 500 most variable genes (a two-sample PCA is degenerate, so it is replaced by the equivalent two-sample diagnostics); (T1S2) median-of-ratios size-factor normalization inside DESeq2 with the low-count pre-filter (>=10 counts in at least 1 sample, the smallest group size), then a purely DESCRIPTIVE ranked table of log2(treated/control) on normalized counts, with the reference level set explicitly to the control condition so a positive log2FC means higher in treated - no p-values, no FDR, no 'significant gene' calls; (T1S3) a report that states the method, package versions, the contrast, the number of genes retained, the ranking cut used, and, prominently, that this design cannot establish differential expression and what design would (>=3 biological replicates per condition). One further caveat propagates from the profile: the counts are 'from salmon as delivered' with no statement of whether the length correction occurred, and no per-sample quant.sf files or average-transcript-length table are present in the inputs. Per R-0169@18ab the counts are therefore used as delivered with no length offset, tximport is NOT run on a gene table, and the report must state that the length offset is lost and that a shift in isoform usage can masquerade as expression change. No enrichment step is planned: the research question asks only for differentially expressed genes, and running gene-set enrichment on an unreplicated, untested ranking would manufacture pathway claims from a fold-change list with no error control.

steps.method: blind VST, PCA on top variable genes, sample distance heatmap
descriptive log2 fold change of normalized counts, no inferential test
method, versions, design, thresholds, n_tested, session_info
